question: As per the 2011 Census, what is the density of the population of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**382 persons/km2**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• India is one of the **nations **with the **highest population densities**.
 
• The number of people** per square kilometre** is considered** population density.**
 
• The average population density across the globe was **15 persons per square kilometre.**
 
• India's population density in the year **2011** was **382 people per square kilometre.**
 
• The state with the densest population density is **Bihar**, with **1,106 people per square kilometre**, followed by **West Bengal (1,028) **and **Kerala **(860)**.** 
 
• Between **1991** and **2011**, population density **rose **in all **States **and **Union Territories**. 
 
• With a decadal growth rate of 17.72 percent, India's population density in the year 2011 was 382 persons per square kilometre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• 
 India is one of the **oldest civilizations **in the world, with a **kaleidoscope **of different cultures.
 
 
• 
 Its **socioeconomic standing **has generally increased since it **gained independence**.
 
 
• 
 India, the **seventh**-**largest nation **in the **world**, is divided from the **Asian **continent by hills and the ocean, giving its government a distinct **geographic entity**.
